text_fidelity_a:
Kodak PlayFull ZE2 Waterproof Video Camera with 2x Optical Zoom and 2-Inch LCD Screen (Black) I made absolutely sure everything was closed before putting it into water, not that one could have much faith in the mechanisms keeping it closed, as they are easy to accidentally open. I put it in the water gently, and only a foot or so, to film some stingrays and fish; this recording went fine. Later that day, I wanted to photograph a tiny little crab. I took one picture from above the water, and one from below. I noticed this time, when I put the camera underwater, that bubbles started to come out the top. I immediately took it out and noticed the screen starting to fog up with condensation and moisture, the first very bad sign. I double checked everything was still closed, and it was. No part of it had been opened. I put it back in, hoping for the best. After coming back to the sand (never having done more than a few feet underwater), I tried to turn it on to get some video. It would not turn on. I checked again, and nothing appeared to be open. I then dried the exterior and opened it, only to discover there was water on the inside. I immediately removed the SD card, in hopes of salvaging it, but the camera was (is) completely dead.

Two days later, there is corrosion forming on the inside from the water, but at least I salvaged the content on the SD card. The results? Video quality is fine above and below water. Photo quality is a mess. Absolutely the worst pics imaginable.
I am so glad I didn't have to pay for this product; I would have been furious it didn't even last a day in the ocean.

I expected more, since I had previously purchased a "Kodak EasyShare Sport C123 12 MP Waterproof Digital Camera", which has been great! That product never failed after much abuse and takes decent picture and video. I'm not sure what happened here, but buyer beware! Try the EasyShare Sport instead.

I'll post some pictures and, if it lets me, some video too. I hope you all find this helpful!

UPDATE: I can't post video (sorry)
Also, I looked at some other reviews that mentioned water getting in while at the pool or in other non-salinated water. Bear in mind that many electronics can survive water immersion if it is fresh water (as opposed to salt water). Many of these reviewers gave the camera more than one star because it was able to work again, but bear in mind this will NOT hold true it Salt water enters the device. Please consider this.
text_fidelity_b: Kodak PlayFull ZE2 Waterproof Video Camera with 2x Optical Zoom and 2-Inch LCD Screen (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Sony HDR-PJ380/W High Definition Handycam Camcorder with 3.0-Inch LCD (White) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) While I'm quite comfortable using an SLR, I've not been all that handy with a camcorder in the past. It's been a few years since I used one, so I was curious to see if user-friendliness has kept pace with technological advancements.

With this model it has. I found it very easy to use right out of the box with just some minor trial and error. I did end up reading the manual (which is pretty decent) but the main functions were pretty self apparent by just fiddling around with it a bit. The menu structure is logical and well presented; the screen is clear and easy to view.

The overall build quality is excellent. It feels more substantial in hand than I expected at this price point while retaining a very lightweight and easy to carry profile. I like the button placement - feels very natural in hand.

I love having the internal memory for storage as well as the little touches, such as a built-in USB connector. These features help make this a grab-and-go type of device, which increases the likelihood and ease of bringing it along and capturing video. (Note: you can also use a plug-in memory card should you want to.)

The video quality in good light/outdoors is excellent - very sharp and clear. Low-light performance is a somewhat grainy but quite decent. Stills are pretty decent. It won't put an SLR to shame, but it's more than good enough for casual snapshots. The internal mic works well and is more immune to wind noise than I expected.

My only significant disappointment with the cam is the projector. Wonderful idea, but the actual performance is lackluster. The projected video is hard to see clearly if there's any appreciable amount of light in the room. The 100 inch projection spec is wildly optimistic if you expect to actually see what is being projected.

Given that this cam does everything else so well, is so easy to use, and a breeze to tote along, I won't detract any stars due to the shortcomings of the projector feature. This is a great cam for the novice cam user (such as myself) or even an intermediate user. However, if the projection feature is a primary need, this may not be a good cam for your needs.
text_fidelity_b: Sony HDR-PJ380/W High Definition Handycam Camcorder with 3.0-Inch LCD (White) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

2. Both units have power switches. While it's annoying to turn them off after each use, at least you can be sure the batteries aren't draining needlessly.

text_fidelity_a:
VIVO Mobile TV Cart for 13 to 50 inch Screens up to 44 lbs, LCD LED OLED 4K Smart Flat and Curved Monitor Panels, Rolling Stand, Locking Wheels, Max VESA 200x200, Black, STAND-TV07W This Vivo Mobile TV Rolling Floor Stand is a tremendous value. It is strong steel, well finished and just right for rolling my 40" Vizio (which weighs only 17 lbs) around the patio for outdoor viewing at the optimal position and height. It looks great and functions flawlessly. It assembled easily. Though it comes with a sheetmetal wrench and a 4mm Allen, I used my own 8mm and 10mm sockets to speed assembly. And a 17mm end wrench to tighten the caster jam nuts. Sadly, one tiny nut was missing; I found a replacement from my personal metric collection of miscellaneous nuts and bolts. Pay close attention to the graphical instructions. I assembled the base upside down before realizing it was wrong. Easily remedied. Also comes with a collection of TV mounting screws, washers and spacers.

I was going to mount the TV on the wall, but being off to the side and quite high, that would very much limit viewing angles and no doubt strain necks. What I really wanted was to have the TV in front of me, wherever I might be sitting and also be able to optimize for group viewing if necessary.

This little cart is exactly what I wanted. It has 2" high quality urethane casters that roll effortlessly and silently on smooth surfaces. They aren't cheap hard plastic wheels. Each caster's threaded stem screws into a tapped hole. A jam nut on the threaded stem allows you to adjust the casters so all four are on the ground, then tighten the jam nuts to lock the adjustment. No wobble! You'll need a 17mm end wrench to tighten the nuts. Two of the casters are equipped with all-lock brakes that prevent both rolling and castering so the TV stays put if desired. When I'm done, I can simply roll the TV out of the way or into the house for safe storage.The base measures 18x20 inches. My 40" TV is 36" wide. You might think it would be top heavy or unstable, but it's not for me, especially as I have the mast set to near its lowest position.

The sturdy steel telescoping mast allows me to lower the TV so that the bottom edge of the 40" TV is 24" inches from the ground -- a few inches above coffee table height. This allows a very comfortable viewing angle when sitting in my somewhat lower patio chairs. In other words, it puts the TV at a very comfortable height to avoid neck strain.

The mount is adjustable and accommodates the 200x200mm Visa mount hole pattern on my TV. It can also handle 100x200 or smaller. Other stands have very large mounting bars. This one is small, simple and compact. Be aware its max Visa mount pattern is 200x200. You can adjust for level and tilt. It can tilt up about 15 degrees. It does not tilt down. The tilt is controlled by a knob. Be aware the TV is more or less permanently mounted onto the mast and the mast is bolted tightly to the base using five fasteners with locknuts: it does not come apart easily. If you want to disassemble this device for travel, you'll need to add thumbscrews.

I did not want extraneous things like extra shelves for a DVD player. It's clean and simple. Its price is very reasonable. With all the nuts and bolts tightened securely, there is no wobble anywhere.

Couldn't he happier. it's well engineered, strong, lightweight and portable.
text_fidelity_b: VIVO Mobile TV Cart for 13 to 50 inch Screens up to 44 lbs, LCD LED OLED 4K Smart Flat and Curved Monitor Panels, Rolling Stand, Locking Wheels, Max VESA 200x200, Black, STAND-TV07W

Pangea Audio Vulcan TT Turntable Stand with Vinyl Record Storage - Black Some appear to have had some difficulty or confusion with assembly, but I did it solo fairly quickly with no issues and found the instructions very clear. No tools were needed and all of the pieces went on smoothly. The direction sheet clearly shows and lists what pieces to use. I guess some didn’t see that one of the shelf sections is thicker. The stand appears quite sturdy and stable. Yes, the only real issue is if you’re using the discs at the feet. I guess the bare, spike type feet ends are supposed to be for thick carpet. Like many I had mine on wood/laminate flooring and so need the small discs as the spike tips will surely scratch it up. This isn’t really a problem per se, but it is quite finicky and it the only part of the operation my wife had to assist with. It definitely would’ve been nice if they’d just included both a spike and attached foot type tips with the stand especially at this price. I included two pics with this review that I took while in the process of getting it and components situated. The stand easily fits my vintage Sansui 661 receiver on the middle shelf and Audio Technica LP120 turntable on the top. I hope both this review and photos showing it with the perspective of having components on it help.

Edit: So, yea, I did dock a star due to the feet issue. As I noted they are finicky, but can quickly get frustrating. While I had to move the stand around getting my stereo stuff sorted the small discs constantly came off and you just really can’t put them back in solo. They will and did put small indentations on my floor with the discs off. My solution was to pick up a 4 pack of 1” sliders from WM that are plastic on the bottom with an adhesive disc on the top. I then stuck the small metal discs from the stand on the slider. Once my wife helped me place the discs back on the legs it could then slide pretty freely and they stayed on. It’s a shame they didn’t include a normal leg along with the pins. I still like the stand quite a bit, but I’d warn people with mobility issues against this one even as nice as it is.
text_fidelity_b: Pangea Audio Vulcan TT Turntable Stand with Vinyl Record Storage - Black

text_fidelity_a:
G.G.Martinsen Crystal-faceted 8 GB Mini Usb Port Multi-lingual Selection 1.8 LCD Mp3/Mp4, Video Player, Music Player, Media Player, Video player, Audio player With a Slot for a micro SD card--Black I have been offered three different G.G. Martinsen players free or at a discount in exchange for my honest review. I like this one better than the first one I got ([[ASIN:B0173CW2CQ an 8GB player]]), but because I went into detail in that review on the different functions (that this one also has), I've copied the functional descriptions from that review below. I'll just compare this one to the pink one in terms of what's different.

I like the black color of this, the ability to put it on a keychain or lanyard, and how small it is, but I don't like the way it all handles nearly as much as I do the [[ASIN:B0168C6MB4 16 GB player]] that I will review separately. The controls and settings are just awfully fiddly and not terribly intuitive. That you can add up to 16GB extra memory via an SDHC card (for a total of 24GB) is a boon, and that's the only thing I like better about this player than the 16GB one; the latter does not have an expansion slot. It's a useful thing if using a player like this when exercising if you can swap out different kinds of music for different types of activity—what works for running or walking will be different than what you'd use for swimming or dancing, for example. But still, these players all hold a decent amount of music natively, and you can also copy a ton of files to it if you're using it to double as a flash drive.

Here's the original functional review for this type of player:

The first thing I tried was the FM radio, because I was really doubtful it was going to work very well in my bedroom, but I was able to pull in NPR and the voices were crystal-clear. The earphones that come with this look really cheap, but they sound pretty good. As with any earphones, they don't cancel surrounding sounds, which makes them perfect for going out for a nice brisk walk. I actually prefer earphones to earbuds because earbuds never fit my ears right. These are like the original Apple earphones, and they stay in my smaller ears really well. I think it's a nice touch that these earphones are included with the player because you can use them in situations where you don't want your really good headphones to get lose or ruined. The device has the following menus, accessible by pressing the Menu button, then the right play button to cycle through them.

SETUP: It's very fiddly trying to set these settings. It takes a lot of trial and error to get it all to work. These are the settings: Clock, LCD Set (not sure what this is), Language (came set to English), Power Off (I can't figure out how to get into these settings to set the times to zero so the player doesn't shut off too soon, so this is why I'm knocking it back to three stars), an Online Mode, Firmware Upgrades, Memory Info.

MUSIC: Navigating through music is straightforward cycling through folders and files. I set up a Walking Songs folder and also dragged my whole Collective Soul Folder with Subfolders to the device, and I was able to navigate between the folders before playing. Selecting specific songs is more difficult. I've never learned how to create playlist files (I know, I know), so I can't say if those will work. There is a funky little equalizer animation on the screen when you play a song.

VIDEO: There's actually a nice music video included on the device, and it will play over and over if you don't stop it. I can see that this might make it possible to put together a loop of items to keep a child entertained on a trip, but it might also have utility for studying, memory work, a flash-card-like experience, or the like.

RECORDER: What it is. Records in .wav format at 32kbps. Great for quick reminders or embarrassing your friends.

VOICE: Used to play back recordings.

FM RADIO: Works great on the stations I've tried, without an antenna of any kind. I may have to start listening to more radio while I'm working.

PHOTO: A simple photo viewer, so you can keep all the pictures of your pets or kids that you'd normally have in your wallet to inflict on the people you meet. I'm just learning about QR codes (scanned my first one on my phone the other day), but I would think you could generate QR codes to carry on this device as well. The device does not recognize .png or .eps files, but it reads .jpgs fine, even larger ones (which do take a bit more time to load).

EBOOK: This is for reading simple .txt files. Don't think you can put anything proprietary like Kindle ebooks on it; it didn't read the .mobi file I copied onto it, or the .epub, or the .pdf. But who'd want to read a whole big book on such a tiny screen anyway? Use the EBOOK capability to take grocery lists or short paragraphs of instructions with you.

GAMES: I almost forgot the games. I'm not a game player. There are a handful of games that I haven't bothered to look at.

This player is not a super-fancy high-end piece of electronics, but it's a lot of bang for the buck and also something you wouldn't die over if you happened to lose it. Of course, you can always use it instead of a flash drive to take files with you different places for subsequent transfer. So it's a lot of functionality in one small package.
text_fidelity_b: G.G.Martinsen Crystal-faceted 8 GB Mini Usb Port Multi-lingual Selection 1.8 LCD Mp3/Mp4, Video Player, Music Player, Media Player, Video player, Audio player With a Slot for a micro SD card--Black

text_fidelity_a:
Linksys N300 Wi-Fi Wireless Router (E900) As a wireless router, this works pretty much like any other, so I thought I'd use it for another purpose: wireless networking between computers in a household that does not have internet (since this is the situation for many people).
For that usage, here's the review:

Appearance: This is a very streamline wireless router with 4 hardline ports. It's small and flat, good for a desk. The problems I have with the design are that it HAS to lie flat, and you can't mount it on a wall. Depending on how cluttered your desk area is may cause some issues.
-3 out of 5 stars

Setup: This router comes with a generic setup CD which assists not so tech savvy users to setup their wireless network using minor cables and a CD. During the CD installation it has "Show Me" buttons to assist users on actions they need to take. A large problem with this router is that you can't setup the router without an active internet connection. I attempted to use the 192.168.1.1 to manually setup the router without using the CD and was met with obstruction requiring me to run their software. This would be a bad router for local home groups without an internet connection. Attempted to connect wirelessly and was granted access to setup things like the security to connect, the security options are minor and only seem to allow WPA2-Personal security with the standard AES encryption. Because this is intended more for internet than networking, this won't count much against the overall product, so
-3 out of 5

Usability: I did the connection with my laptop and walked around to see if the signal would drop. I made it out to the street corner from where the router was placed, this was about 200ft. I still received a single bar signal out at the corner. A recommendation for the router if you are using it to broadcast an internet signal that it is password protected using both letters UPPERCASE and lowercase with numbers and symbols. This will help protect your network and any data stored on your computers. Even though the range on this router was pretty good the minor security options make it difficult to give it above a 3 out of 5.
-3 out of 5

Reliability: I attempted to reset the router back to factory by resetting it and letting it sit for about 15minutes. The router kept all information including the Name and the Password. This is both good and bad if there is a short power outage you don't have to worry about resetting passwords and the router information however if you ever lose your password you might not be able to restore it back to factory.
-3 out of 5
text_fidelity_b: Linksys N300 Wi-Fi Wireless Router (E900)

text_fidelity_a:
Canary Pro Indoor Home Security Camera 1080p HD WiFi IP | 24/7 Watch Live Video, Siren, Climate Monitor, Motion Alerts, Two-Way Talk, Night Vision, 10x Zoom, Private Mode, Works with Alexa and More Doesn't live up to the hype. The image quality is not great unless you're right in front of the camera. I placed mine on the tv console, which is on the far side of the room, and has the best views of the living and high traffic areas. You know, where you actually want surveillance...

First unless someone is within 3 feet of the camera, you can't make out faces.

Second the time delay between canary detecting movement and notifying me of activity has been 15 and 30 minutes, including when I've been in the house. When I was out of state, the delay was 15 min. When I was in my own home but in night mode, the delay was 30 min. So I'm not sure how this would be effective in notifying the police because it would give robbers plenty of time to clear out your house before you even see it.

Third you need to be aware of the location you place it and the natural shadows that occur throughout the day. I was getting notifications every 10 minutes. So I changed the sensitivity, but I still get notifications.

I think the concept is great, but the technology has a long way to go.
text_fidelity_b: Canary Pro Indoor Home Security Camera 1080p HD WiFi IP | 24/7 Watch Live Video, Siren, Climate Monitor, Motion Alerts, Two-Way Talk, Night Vision, 10x Zoom, Private Mode, Works with Alexa and More

HAOHUNT Camcorder Digital Video Camera HD 1080P 30fps 3.0 INCH Touch Screen 24MP Camcorder with Microphone and Wide Angle Lens Vlogging Camera with Remote Control Infrared Night Vision Recorder This digital camcorder has features not found on many camcorders.
First the things I like about this Camcorder:
This camcorder records in high definition (1020 at 30 fps), and two low resolution (720P at both 30 and 60 fps) select-able from the screen.
There is a option for setting the camera up for motion control triggered recording.
The system has a IR based night vision system to record in total blackout conditions.
The remote can be used to control most modes of the camcorder and start/stop recording.
This system comes with a external mic to help in recording the audio component of your filming, you have the option to use this mic or not depending on your circumstances.
You can use the camcorder as a photo camera with resolutions ranging from 5mp to 24mp along with settings for white balance, color, and shutter speeds.
You can turn off the beep sound for camera functions, something you may use if recording wildlife.
This Camcorder comes with a wide view lens, great when recording in a shallow area such as a room to get everyone and everything into one shot.
Extra battery, handy for extended use or areas where you cannot recharge the camera.

Things I would like to see improved:
The zoom is digital only, not an optical zoom. This limits the camcorder to recording only items in a shallow depth, not great for outdoor use unless you are up close to your subject.

All in all, a decent camcorder for use where you are close (physically) to your subject, or as long as you understand its limitations.

GIGABYTE Z690 Gaming X (LGA 1700/ Intel Z690/ ATX/ DDR5/ Quad M.2/ PCIe 5.0/ USB 3.2 Gen2X2 Type-C/ 2.5GbE LAN/Gaming Motherboard) Compared to the Strix-E and Carbon, this is definitely the best of the three. Only issue is the coil whine, which is a roll of the dice. Worst case scenario it'll whine all the time like the first one I tried, whereas my newest replacement only does it during memory tests - which is acceptable.

But other than that, it's excellent. The Carbon and Strix-E both had issues getting my 7200 kit stable at XMP, and I spent almost a week straight tweaking voltages on the Strix - it would always eventually error out in Karhu after 30-60 minutes or so. The Master however is rock solid, and I was able to OC to 7400cl34 with extreme stability. Its "Low Latency/High Bandwidth" options are excellent, and perform better than the XMP tweaked setting on the ASUS.

It also ran the 13900k the coolest, and seemed easier to get stable. Overall if you are lucky enough to not have one with coil whine, it's definitely the best option in this price range.

ZAGG Limitless, Full-Size Multi-Device Universal Bluetooth Backlit Keyboard - Black I've been getting to the point where I have multiple tablets and mobile devices around the house that occasionally benefit from having a physical keyboard. I like that this one lets me switch between three paired devices with the push of a button.

It feels sturdy and the keys have a pleasant texture. It's bigger than previous bluetooth keyboards I've tried, which I think is in keeping with it being designed to be used with multiple devices. It's also kind of heavy, so it seems more like an around the house keyboard than a portable.

I like it better as an occasional keyboard than one to use all the time. it's too flat to feel ergonomic. The alt and command keys on the bottom row are all double size, which feels like a designer wanted a big space bar but didn't want to leave any empty space anywhere. The result is that they are easy to bump, which can send you off into menus. The slot for standing up a device on the back of the keyboard feels a bit close, and not wide enough for my Surface tablet in landscape mode, and portrait mode makes it fall over, so the stand is likely only good for things up to small tablet size.

text_fidelity_a:
Lifeproof FRĒ SERIES iPhone 6/6s Waterproof Case (4.7" Version) - Retail Packaging - SUNSET (PIPELINE/WINDSURF/LONGBOARD) I got my mother the Lifeproof FRE case for her iPhone 6. For the last year, she’s been using a cheap case I bought on Amazon, the Diztronic Voyeur Case. I didn’t feel it was protective enough, so I hoped the Lifeproof FRE would work for her.

Unfortunately, she didn’t like the case at all, and wanted it off her phone minutes after I put it on. I made her use it for a few weeks, and while she didn’t experience any sound problems, there were several quality of life things that sealed the dislike for the Lifeproof FRE case.

PRO:
—The built-in screen protector is pretty good. I liked that I didn’t have to install it myself, as it’s part of the case.

CONS:
—Within minutes of putting the Lifeproof FRE case on her phone, I dropped it. The back of the case is slick, some kind of hard plastic instead of the grippier TPU case. The Lifeproof case just didn’t feel nice to hold in my hand, and with the slicker plastic, I worried that my mom would drop her phone as well.

—The little “door” that protects the charger port was super hard for her to open. Every time my mom wanted to charge her phone, I had to come do it for her, since she couldn’t get the door open. I understand needing a tight seal for the waterproof protection, but there has to be an easier way to access the charger port.

—The small oval cut out for charging cords was too small for my non Apple Lightning cables. I have two that are Apple certified, AmazonBasics and Zerolemon, and neither fit.

—My mom found it impossible to manipulate any of the buttons. I assume the buttons will loosen up over months, but boy, they are super hard to press when the case is new.

My mom’s not quite the intended audience for the case, but as she plans to keep her iPhone for a few years, we want it to stay in nice shape. And you never know when you’re going to drop your phone into a snowbank or puddle, so having a waterproof case adds peace of mind. But I’ll have to keep looking for her, because the Lifeproof FRE had a couple of little problems that added up to big annoyances.
text_fidelity_b: Lifeproof FRĒ SERIES iPhone 6/6s Waterproof Case (4.7" Version) - Retail Packaging - SUNSET (PIPELINE/WINDSURF/LONGBOARD)

text_fidelity_a:
RayHom 8 Bay AA AAA Battery Charger, Double Charging Speed with LCD Display Independent Slot for Ni-MH AA AAA Rechargeable Batteries This is a nice alternative to chargers that require you to charge batteries in pairs. There are spaces for eight batteries, and you can charge any number within them, and mix and match AA and AAA. The eight spaces are divided electrically into two banks of four spaces, and the manufacturer says each bank can provide 2000 mA of charging power (which lowers as you add more batteries and the current is divided between them). However, the included adapter only provides only 1200 mA (so says its label), so I'm not sure the math checks out.

I gave it a test with an assortment of different brand and capacity rechargeables, then checked the batteries with a multimeter. Even fully loaded the charger worked pretty quickly and brought each one up to just over 1.4 volts. I have a brand-name charger that will bring them up to 1.5 volts, but that may be overcharging a bit and might reduce overall battery life.

The one minor negative is that the battery icons on the backlit display are pretty much invisible unless you bend down or tilt the charger up to see them. You can see how low the angle is in the photo I uploaded.

Other than that, convenient and reasonably fast, it's a nice charger.
text_fidelity_b: RayHom 8 Bay AA AAA Battery Charger, Double Charging Speed with LCD Display Independent Slot for Ni-MH AA AAA Rechargeable Batteries

SABRE Home Security Personal Safety Kit, Comes With A 120 dB Doorstop Alarm, 120 dB Door Or Window Alarm And A 120 dB Personal Alarm, Safety Essentials For College Students, Home Owners and Travelers With crime rates going up in NYC, this is an ideal kit for anyone living in an apartment, especially if they're alone and elderly. It covers two areas most vulnerable to thieves: your window and the door, while the key chain is best for when you're coming home late at night on a dark, lonely street. Just pull the pin and the alarm screams.

Of the three items, I would say the window alarm rates highest in terms of usefulness. In fact, I wish this set came with three of them. We travel a lot, and the biggest fear we have is intruders breaking in through our high-rise window, as we have a fire escape near one of them.

The door stop is the least useful to me as a thief would have to break through one of our windows first before going through a door. My front door is already secured by locks and the other doors in our place generally remain open. I suppose we could reinforce the front door with the doorstop, but it seems like overkill. If you lived in a dorm and wanted a particular room to be off-limits, I suppose it would be useful in that case. This item reminds me of the alarm that would be set off if you used an emergency exit. As if in acknowledgement that this item won't be used as much as the others, no battery was supplied for it, unlike the others.

As for the key chain, this is one of those devices that will lay dormant for long periods (knock on wood). You'll have to remember to check and test the batteries occasionally because it will be rarely used.

Overall, for the price this set can't be beat. It feels more like a "sampler" pack, though, as it has only one of each product when multiples of each one would have been more helpful.
text_fidelity_b: SABRE Home Security Personal Safety Kit, Comes With A 120 dB Doorstop Alarm, 120 dB Door Or Window Alarm And A 120 dB Personal Alarm, Safety Essentials For College Students, Home Owners and Travelers

text_fidelity_a:
Fujifilm Instax Wide 300 Instant Film Camera (Black) Boy! does this camera remind me of my old Polaroid Square Shooter. This camera is NOTHING like your iPhone camera as it's big, and totally analog except for the film counter on the back. I love it when the motor runs and film comes sliding out - a sound I well remember. I think the hardest thing about using this camera was getting the shoulder strap put on, other than that it's very easy to use. Though it is on the big side, it doesn't weigh much and the view finder and shutter button are pretty much intuitive. I'm left handed so holding it like a right-hander took a little getting used too, but it's not a problem for me. This camera is made for right-handers so those who are very much left-handed might not like the way you have to hold it, and the shutter button is on the right side front. It has flash and you can adjust the light/dark and distance to you subject with minimal effort.

Loading the film was easy, aiming at my subject was easy, the shutter button was easy to depress and everything is/was easy. The close-up adapter looks like there's no way it will attach itself to the lens, but somehow it does. I took one close-up of my dog but the picture didn't turn out very good because she moved away right when I hit the shutter button-but that's typical for her. I haven't taken a "selfie" yet but it seems like it will be easy to do.

The color development of the film is pretty good. I took a wide angle picture of my raised garden beds and I was able to get all of them in the picture and the various green colors were vivid. I also took a picture of the front of our house, and though I had to still walk across the street to our neighbor's driveway to get the entire house in the view finder, the picture turned out nice. Again, the colors were bright and vivid. It got the entire house plus some area on both sides. In the past with my other cameras I would have to get further away or be happy with just most of the house in the picture so it's real nice to get the whole thing with room to spare.

The film is kind of pricey. For a pack of 40 pictures it costs around $34.00. I figured it would be kind of expensive and I hope the price of the film goes down some. This is a comfort camera for those of us who grew up with Polaroids. It may be that since we are living in highly uncertain and stressful times, having a camera like this is a cool blast from the past and may make us just feel better having one like this, plus it takes nice pictures.
text_fidelity_b: Fujifilm Instax Wide 300 Instant Film Camera (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Pivotal Living Tracker 1 (2nd Generation) Black (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I came to this tracker cold. The Housemate has a Fitbit, but I never used it, and really haven't paid a lot of attention to what it did so I had no expectations of what the Pivotal Living tracker might do. However before I tell you what I discovered, let me explain some things about myself. I'm in my sixties, and have a sedentary job. I would like to be more active, I would like to compare my actual sleep habits against what I perceive them to be, I would like to keep an eye on hydration. I have some other goals, but these are the main ones that apply to my use of the tracker.

So how does the Pivotal Living tracker stand up to these goals? First off, because so much of my everyday movement is not easily measurable by the tracker, I'm not really getting an accurate step count. (Moving around the house holding things doesn't always register. Sitting and doing something like folding laundry sometimes does.) This is a bit of a problem because it makes it difficult to estimate how I'm doing on my step goal. So, accuracy in step count? Not so much. Going to stick to a pedometer or pedometer app. C, maybe C+ because I can set my own goals based on my health and how my day is going. (Right now I have a torn meniscus, and all my steps are limping or cane-assisted. Not fun, and not conducive to accurate step counts.)

Hydration? Great, unless you forget to enter an amount until after midnight. Whoops, sorry, can't add anything to your daily total. This is a huge oversight IMO. I sometimes finish my daily amount late in the evening when I'm not thinking about using the mobile app. However, the process of tracking it on your own is a good one. They simply need to fix the access problem. B+

Daily activity. Honestly I have NO clue how this is tracked. I'd have thought it was step-based, but I've never yet had daily activity show up on my dashboard, so there has to be some other way this band tracks activity. However, having an activity alarm that reminds me to stop what I'm doing, get up and walk around for a few minutes... that's immensely valuable to me. Without it, I'd simply forget and keep on writing or editing. I'm going to give it an A because I love the alarm which can be set for 20/40/or 60 minutes.

The rest? Sleep alarm... I've been wakened by this exactly once, when I was very nearly awake anyway. Every other morning it's done zip. I'll wake up an hour later and think, "Wha?" It's back to my clock radio. C, at best. However the sleep tracker seems surprisingly accurate based on what I remember of my nights. It fairly accurately charts how many times I've woken up, and how much good sleep I've gotten. I find this quite reassuring. A, even A+.

Calories burned: Since this is both step and activity based, it's pretty useless for me. Anyway, my goal isn't about calories, it's about activity, so I'm not going to grade this part of the app. Also, weight: Clearly this is another sub-app like hydration, which requires you to input your numbers. It keeps my weight in front of me which is a good thing, but it's not really something I feel I can adequately grade.

Problem: If you take it off it will turn itself off. I tried to put it on my desk when I was typing since it interfered with the position of my wrist. I could hear the activity alert when the band buzzed against the desk, but then it stopped because the tracker had shut down. I thought it was out of juice and couldn't figure out why I was getting less than 24 hours on the battery. When I finally figured it out, I had to start wearing it up high on my arm. Fortunately the band is big enough to allow it to sit several inches above my wrist.

Price: Very, very good. I recognize that the modest cost of the tracker is intended to get you to buy the yearly subscription, but I don't mind that. If the service works, I'm happy to pay $1 a month for it. That's still minor league stuff. However I get frequent errors saying that the goal information can't be updated from the site, and I get odd readings on my dashboard. However, by the end of the day it's usually sorted itself out, so I don't have a lot of quibbles so far.

Overall, and taking price into account I think I'd give this a B, at least for my needs. It reminds me of the things I need to remember to do, and it gives me a place where I can keep track of those goals. The cost to do this is, as I indicated, quite modest. If you're not ready to drop a lot of money on a more sophisticated tracker, give the Pivotal Living tracker a try.

Note: I'm using this on a Fire phone, which means I had to side-load the app. The instructions on how to install Google Play and everything else you need to side load Google Play apps are available on You Tube, and it's dead easy. Once you've done that, just go to the Play Store and download the Pivotal Living app, and have at it.
text_fidelity_b: Pivotal Living Tracker 1 (2nd Generation) Black (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

JVC HAECX20B Sports Clip Inner Ear Headphones, Black The sound quality of these earbuds AKA headphones is excellent. They are exactly what they are advertised to be, earbuds with clips that go over the ears to keep them from falling out of your ears when you are engaged in activities that cause a lot of moving and shaking of your head, which would dislodge ordinary earbuds.

I don't personally engage in sports that strenuous, but but I did thoroughly test these Sports Clips by bending over, hopping up and down and generally moving my head a lot. They did not come loose from my ears.

I found another excellent use for them as well. When I have normal earbuds plugged in when I am baking bread or other dishes that get my hands very messy, all too frequently non-clip earbuds begin to slip out of my ears. Its a real pain to have to wash sticky dough off my hands and dry them before I can stuff the loose earbuds back into my ears. I don't have that problem at all with these Sports Clips earbuds, and that's very convenient.

The one flaw with this product, at least it's a flaw to me, because it doesn't make any sense and is somewhat uncomfortable, is the way the cord is designed. It is not coequal in length on both sides. One side is about four times longer than the other. There also isn't any sliding plastic piece that allows you to adjust the length of the splitting of the cord so that the user can adjust how wide it gaps over one's throat and chest, which would allow the user to opt, as desired, to even tighten it right up under the chin.

Other than those issues, this is an excellent product.

text_fidelity_a:
Acer Aspire R 15 2-in-1 Laptop, 15.6" Full HD Touch, 7th Gen Intel Core i7, GeForce 940MX, 12GB DDR4, 256GB SSD, R5-571TG-7229 This will be a fairly detailed and honest review.

1. Who is this for?
This computer is what I would consider a gateway computer. Those who are looking at upgrading a fairly old or not so powerful laptop and are looking to do a little more productivity, this is a great option.

2. What do you get?
Well you can probably read the description, however it's worth noting. You get an Intel i7 7500u CPU (dual core with 4 threads) 12gb DDR4 RAM, Nvidia 940mx GPU, a 256gb SSD, 15.6" 1080p screen, fingerprint reader, and a backlit keyboard.

The reason I mention all of the feautures is because you would be hardpressed to find another laptop with these features for the same price. To my knowledge there is not laptop on the market for $800 with an i7, dedicated graphics, 12gb of RAM and an SSD. This is really one of the best values on the market right now.

With all of that said, this isn't for everyone. If you want to do extensive gaming, this is not for you. Can it game? Yes, light gaming can be achieved, however it isn't marketed as a gaming laptop. Is this for someone who wants to do editing (video, audio, photos)? Yes, again light editing can be achieved.

What blew me away with this computer is the speakers! They are fantastic! I usually use headphones and would consider myself somewhat picky with sound, and for laptop speakers these are really something great.

This computer is really a middle of the pack all arounders dream. If you dabble in a little of this and a little of that but don't do anything professionally or extremely serious, this is really all you need.

Also, everyone's experience is different. Some hate loud fans, and if this is pushed the fans will be audible. Some don't like that the backlit keyboard times out after 30 seconds of no use. These things really don't bother me.

Lastly, the versatility of this laptop is really great. I've bought tablets and sold them because I couldn't justify having a laptop and tablet, then bought tablets again because I missed the things I could do with them that I was missing on a laptop. This solved all of those issues except size. It's pretty big, which for some is a plus others its not.

Overall, if you are looking at upgrading and don't want to spend $1,200-2,000 on a flagship model laptop this is a great option! I can't recommend this enough.
text_fidelity_b: Acer Aspire R 15 2-in-1 Laptop, 15.6" Full HD Touch, 7th Gen Intel Core i7, GeForce 940MX, 12GB DDR4, 256GB SSD, R5-571TG-7229

text_fidelity_a:
HP ENVY Desktop Computer, Intel Core i7-10700, 16 GB RAM, 1 TB Hard Drive & 512 GB SSD Storage, Windows 10 Pro (TE01-1254, 2020 Model) It is an alright system if you are only going to be doing basic computing like Microsoft Office, email, and some Netflix (but maybe not all at the same time). However, at a current price of over $850 being saddle with only the onboard graphics is hardly acceptable. Second, this system is also only okay if you never plan to repair the computer if there are issues with the power supply or motherboard. If you toss out your systems when they break, then this will work. If you like to swap out the bad parts, run for the hills you do not want to be stuck dealing with the HP part store.

If you want to play any games or use programs that require a bit more heavy lifting, (design software, CAD, or anything pulling a bunch of images or rendering) or need to have several programs running at once, you are going to struggle without a graphics card.

But can't you just add your own Graphics Card, I mean it is 2020 after all? Well... while this system does have an open slot on the motherboard for the addition of a graphics card it is severely handicapped in using it. For one, it is a very small case and you will be stuck with a small form factor card, which tend to be more expensive than their standard size counterparts. Worse yet, the included system power is only 180 watts. You cannot run much past whatever is already in the system with that, so you will need to also upgrade the power supply. Here is where it gets annoying. HP not only uses their own motherboard (Baker in this system) but the motherboard uses a proprietary connection to the power supply, so you HAVE TO BUY their power supply and only theirs. There is not an adapter, I looked and looked and looked some more.

That means heading over to the HP parts store website and trying not to pound your head into a wall with how backwards and outdated their system is. If you manage to locate the ONLY 400 watt power supply that works with the baker motherboard (yes 400 watt is the biggest they make that work for this case and motherboard) you will be hit with a $125 price tag (more like $150 after tax and shipping) for a power supply that should really cost half that. Which even if it says is in stock, will likely be back-ordered. They told me I'd be lucky to see it in 2 months even if it says "instock" in the system. Because they are the only ones selling it, you have to either wait or just forget about the upgrade. If you NEED it because your current power supply isn't working, well too bad for you.

If you have hung in this far and managed to get the power supply squared away, you can start on the graphics card piece. Now here is where it gets fun, you will want to avoid the HP parts store. They have the GTX 1660ti listed but its price bounces from over $1000 (yes a grand) to around $700 for a card that is about $300 on Amazon. Due to the power supply limitations a 1660ti is as high as you are going to be able to get, which puts you on par with an entry level gaming laptop. Due to size limitations of the HP Envy case you will want to stick to a small form factor card (generally that means one fan not two, but measure first some of those single fans are still a bit long).

So between the $150 power supply (that you may never get) and the ($300 graphics card off amazon) you are looking at about $450 in an upgrade to basically keep pace with a low level gaming laptop that costs less than what you paid for the HP Envy to begin with.

Which is my biggest problem with this system and the reason for the 3 stars, because it only does what it says (so earns its 3 stars) BUT if it has any sort of hardware issue down the line or doesn't meet your needs, you are going to be stuck buying a whole new system or be left to the mercy of HPs terribly unreliable part store with its over inflated prices and unreliable delivery timetables.
text_fidelity_b: HP ENVY Desktop Computer, Intel Core i7-10700, 16 GB RAM, 1 TB Hard Drive & 512 GB SSD Storage, Windows 10 Pro (TE01-1254, 2020 Model)

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Wireless Reading Device (6" Display, U.S. Wireless) Would like to jump in with first impressions after a short visit with my new Kindle. You wouldn't be here if you were not already excited by the Kindle concept and what it can do. Both are nice as expected. So if I jump right into the critical... Particular bright spots are a familiar store front and truly-fast downloads. (software developer, experienced technology device user).

First concern I noticed is there is lack of grip on this unit. The back is stainless and the front smooth faced, so its hard to hold. The unit is not featherweight, so found the only option to rest the kindle on my legs or belly. Can tuck your pinkies underneath, but that is not sustainable. Kindle 3, please give me some grip.

There is a Next button perfectly placed for your right thumb, but in the same place on the left is a... Next button! English readers are wired to believe left is back and right is forward. Instead, the Prev button is higher up on the left and requires a conscious effort. Next buttons on both thumbs: why?!

Kindle needs a master Enter button, beyond just pressing the control knob. Like most laptop touch-pad users would, I keep finding myself pressing the adjacent "Menu" button as an expected Enter button and going back to where I came from. Frustrating.

The main buttons clunk a bit too much; patrons at the library will know every time you turn a page, which is often. Kindle needs to sit in a Honda for a few minutes and learn how a button should respond to your pressing it. The screen already undertakes an annoying and unnecessary slide-machine-style blackout between screens, so no need to have audible clues to your navigation.

In Text2Speech mode, I turned the Kindle off... the display shut down but the speech went on. That's a QC bug. Had to turn back on, quit the story, then turn off... a major bummer because the Kindle is designed to pick up where you left off, but in this case, now you will have to both reselect the story and re-turn-on speech mode every time. Ouch!

Finally, I mistakenly selected Dutch for Wikipedia, and cannot get back to English Wikipedia. Its cookied in. I know well enough to go to the en. prefix version eventually, but most users won't...

Small gripes include a front white face destined to get very dirty, a lack of face coverplate and low rent AmazonKindle logo quite unworthy of a $360 device.

All these are suggestions for improvement, and not entirely relevent to whether you would buy this unit or not. Booking on !!
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Wireless Reading Device (6" Display, U.S. Wireless)

text_fidelity_a: AMORNO Bluetooth Headphones, Foldable Wireless Neckband Headset with Retractable Earbuds, Sports Sweatproof Noise Cancelling Stereo Earphones with Mic (Grey) True story.. I go through headphones like they are disposable cups.. Honestly this year alone I have bought 14 pairs of headphones.. both neckband and true wireless ones.. I listen to podcasts all day everyday. I always have a headphone in.. I fall asleep with them listening to Synctuition and I listen to a podcast when I wake up for work. The second I'm out of the shower, an earbud goes in.. I have one pair charging at all times so I'm never without.. Being used heavily.. the bands break, the cords breaks, one bud stops working, one bud goes missing, the Bluetooth stops working, the microphone stops working.. the list goes on.. I probably should just buy an expensive pair but honestly I'm convinced I'll just break or lose them.. So I stick with affordable ones until I inevitably break or lose them.. I tell you this to reassure you that I KNOW my headphones.. These have been great so far. The battery on them is killer. I can get two whole days of literal continuous use before the dreaded "battery low" warning. They retract really quickly and smoothly. They are light weight and the sound is great. I will say though, that I am not qualified to judge sound quality.. I usually only have one bud in at a time to be able to drive, work, talk to others and since it's mostly podcasts.. I can't say that the bass is amazing or the treble is whatever.. I do listen to both at night to sleep music and they sound great but again.. not my forte. Endurance and battery life are though and so far these have far surpassed the usual time when I need to replace them.. Great buy for a great price.

text_fidelity_a:
Echo Show - 1st Generation Black I was really surprised by the Show. My first impression was that it's a little bigger than I expected. It's also fairly heavy. Now having used it a few months, I'm glad for the weight. As you are pecking the touch screen with your finger, the extra weight keeps it very stable.

I was anxious to get it started up and see how it's sound compared to my original Echo. I was surprised. I think it sounds better. It has a deeper bass response and the sound is a little more directional with the speakers being in the front.

Other features I really enjoy is that you can load a custom home image, and it constantly scrolls "trending" topics across the home page when not in use. If you see something you want to know more about, you can ask it and it will play the audio or video clip. If you miss something, you can ask it what's trending and it will list everything.

I love that most things you ask it will give the normal Alexa audio response, but also a visual. The weather is a good example. It reads the weather just as an Echo would do, but also shows you the visual on the screen and allows you to scroll through the days ahead with a touch of the finger.

I use it for video calling with a friend who also owns one and it works well. The audio quality is good and we're able to communicate face to face.

I search for and watch youtube videos quite often. If there is something specific you are looking for, it can be painful. The search doesn't always understand slang or complex words, making the search results a little unreliable.

Overall, I really like it. It doesn't "hear" better than the original Echo and does frequently respond when you aren't talking to it, just like the original. It just has a little better sound and a nice touch display screen!
text_fidelity_b: Echo Show - 1st Generation Black

text_fidelity_a:
Azio PRISM USB Wired Keyboard with 7 Colorful Backlights, Black (KB507) Overall, this is a decent full-size USB keyboard. The keys are nicely sized and have a medium length throw. There’s little tactile feedback, making the keys feel rather mushy. But, on the plus side, it’s 100% silent in use – no clicky sound of any type.

The layout is a standard QWERTY with a separate number key pad and F1 to F12 at the top. There’s also a separate pad for cursor up/down/right/left.

The back light is very nice and has the unique feature in that you can change the color. There are several to pick from including a “mixed” mode that has several colors making for a rainbow look. Color selection is easy via a dedicated key at the top of the keyboard. Just press it to cycle through the colors. The back light can also be set to off.

The build quality is decent. It’s all plastic and pretty lightweight, but durable enough for normal use. There’s a kick stand on the back that folds out to prop up the keyboard at a comfortable angle, and non-skid feet to hold it in place. I had no problems with this staying put even when banging away at full typing speed. There is some flex in the frame when typing with force, but nothing horrible.

There’s a small area for resting your palm, but it’s rather short to provide much (if any) ergonomic support.

I've had other similar stoves, including an Ohuhu (?) brand.  That one was nicer in one respect, it had no slotted cross pieces which this one has to space the pot above the flames. I got at least 400 burns out of my last little SS twig stove and i never took any great care to be nice to it...and eventually wore it out.  If i get 400 burns out of this one i'll be a happy guy.  In short, if you are looking for a twig stove to burn what you find on the trail or around camp give this one a try, you'll probably like it.

Defender HD1T4 HD 1080p 4 Channel 1TB Security DVR with Mobile Viewing, Black We couldn't find a way to set this up because of logistics, which is unfortunate. Wireless or Bluetooth options would have worked better for this, not only because of distances, but because having to work with wires at such lengths and hide them in a home would have been beyond unwieldy.

Problem 1: drilling from the exterior of the house to the inside in Florida, unless done by a professional, likely means you created a place for water and moisture to leak in, which inevitably means mold and other issues. Even so, it's understandable that this may be necessary pretty much every time, and perhaps that wouldn't be such a big deal if it weren't for problem 2.

Problem 2: for this to work, you need to have a tv or monitor setup. If you have a bigger space, the distance might be further to get from where you want to record to the place where you have those things.

Here's what would have worked to let us set this up:
Have a hub of some sort that can be put anywhere nearish to the cameras, and then that can connect wirelessly to an app, computer, or monitor on the same network, not just for setup, but in general.

We would have had to go from the garage area to the inside part of the house, somewhere over 70 feet? To get to the nearest tv or monitor.

I'll try again for my small business if we ever change locations, but having to attach to a monitor is a pain. It should be able to work directly from the hub/DVR to an app.

text_fidelity_a:
Klipsch GiG Black Portable Speaker, Black I really wanted to like this speaker. It comes complete with international plugs, an a/c wall charger, and two pouches which I assume is one for the unit and one for the accessories. It is somewhat attractive with a built-in stand that allows you to either place it on its side or in an upright position.

With most speakers, once you have paired it with your device (an Iphone 5s, in my case), you should be all done. This is not so with this unit. The speaker has a spring-loaded slide switch that you push on. It gives you a guitar confirmation tone so that you know that it's working. Now you must go to the "Settings" icon on your device and manually choose the Klipsch speaker. Then you will hear another guitar confirmation tone letting you know that it is paired. You must do this EVERY SINGLE TIME. It is ridiculous. Of course when you turn it off, it will give you yet another guitar confirmation tone.

The sound is very good, but the extra step of always having to re-enable the bluetooth connection through "Settings" totally negates anything positive about this speaker. There is absolutely no reason why my Sony SRSX5 and my JBL Charge automatically pair with my device whenever I turn them on, and yet this one does not. I keep trying to understand why the developers came up with this procedure, but it totally baffles me.

I know that other users have complained in the past about charging issues. Perhaps Klipsch listened to them and fixed this problem because I have not had any difficulties with that.

If you're gonna spend money on a good speaker, please look at the Sony SRSX5. It is an outstanding speaker with logical functions and exceptional sound.
text_fidelity_b: Klipsch GiG Black Portable Speaker, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Fire TV Stick 4K, brilliant 4K streaming quality, TV and smart home controls, free and live TV I’ve had a few Fire TV sticks over the years, and generally I love them. For this model, the first one I got was a dud. It died in 2 days. Amazon took me through some reasonable troubleshooting steps, then replaced it quickly and easily. The second one is a lot better.

In general, I find the remote has a weird tendency to, I guess “rot” is the word. The case starts to feel like it’s covered in a sticky mess. I don’t know why. I guess that’s why the remote covers are so popular. Not a stopping point – they still work – just a point of note. The optional game controllers do not have this issue.

There are ample streaming options. I’ve yet to look for something, even less common things like Wonderium and Funimation, and not find it. The UI is easy to navigate. The device is responsive. I put it through a 7.1 sound system and it can handle that no problem.

A few things to note, not exactly faults of the product, but faults you will encounter while using the product.

For the Disney+ login, the trick of using the phone just errors out and asks to re-authenticate over and over. If you use a strong password, that can be a pain. Once it works, it’s fine, just a pain to set up.

For the Ubisoft+ integration, for many of the games it starts to load then fails. I don’t see the same issue on the same games on PC, so it’s probably related to the app. This was the primary purpose for which I bought the device, so it is a bit of a disappointment. Also note, you need the Luna service for this, which is totally worth it on its own, by the way. Also, at least for me, while the video streaming was fine over WiFi, the gaming required the Ethernet adapter.

It’s not perfect, but it’s outstanding for such a low price. I often use it rather than power up my PS5 to watch Netflix because it is so much more convenient, and of identical quality.
text_fidelity_b: Fire TV Stick 4K, brilliant 4K streaming quality, TV and smart home controls, free and live TV

text_fidelity_a:
Fire HD 10 Tablet with Alexa, 10.1" HD Display, 16 GB, Black - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th) I love everything else Amazon has ever done, so it breaks my heart to write this review. I've had a couple of iPads and they work great, but I find Apple's pricing and politics ridiculous, so I was excited to move away from them and go with an Amazon product. Sadly, the Fire HD is seriously inferior.

This device is SLOW. Every step of the setup process was painfully slow. Downloading, and even opening, apps is slow. I have my OLD iPad sitting right next to the Fire HD performing the same functions on the same WiFi connection and the Fire takes 4 times as long to do anything.

The WiFi connectivity is not great. Again, I have my old iPad 3 sitting right next to this device, and the Fire HD keeps losing the network connection or dropping down to 1-2 bars, while the iPad is streaming and loading everything with lightning speed. Funny thing is, I have a Fire TV Stick running in the same room, and it has a wonderfully reliable, super-fast connection!

The touch screen is also sometimes not very responsive - I will have to tap some things 4-5 times before they trigger.

Most of the apps I was looking for are available in the Amazon App Store. However, these are buggy versions that appear to have been thrown together without the care that the developers have put into their iOs versions.

Possibly the worst part of all is the battery life. We are supposed to get 8 hours of usage.... I get about 4, even with the screen set as dim as possible. It also completely discharges on standby (with NO USE) within 2 days, even with the setting enabled to turn off WiFi when the device is on standby.

I do love the integration with the Amazon ecosystem. I hope someday Amazon will make the necessary improvements and I can give their tablets another chance. But for now, I will be returning this device with a heavy heart. :(
text_fidelity_b: Fire HD 10 Tablet with Alexa, 10.1" HD Display, 16 GB, Black - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th)

text_fidelity_a:
ARCTIC Breeze Pro USB Desktop Fan with 4-Port USB Hub This review covers two different models of the Arctic fan:

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>Model with USB hub:
I have been using the original ARCTIC Breeze for a while and have been very pleased with its performance, and especially pleased with how quiet it runs. The Pro model builds on that and adds a few more useful features.

Unlike the original model which had a bendable stem with a USB plug on the end, the Pro has a base so the fan can be positioned away from the USB port on the PC. The attached power cord is a little over 5 feet long, making it possible to put the fan on my desk and plug it into the PC on the floor.

The base also has 4 USB input ports, so it works as a USB hub. It has a 5V power input jack if you want to turn this into an active hub. The power adapter to do so is NOT included.

Unlike the single-speed original version, this has a knob so you can vary the speed. It's not precise, but there is a somewhat noticeable difference between low and high. It's a continually variable speed - you can turn the dial to whatever speed you like.

Best of all, it's just as quiet, if not quieter, than the original model. That's the biggest plus for me by far, since the cheap USB fans make a racket. This just makes a low-pitched hum. The build quality is solid - the base is sturdy, and the bendable arm holds its position well.

One negative: the packaging. It's in a clam shell package that is a major, major pain to open!

While it's more expensive than the original, the added benefits of being able to position it on a desk and use it as a hub makes the upgrade worth considering. Highly recommend.

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>USA EDITION:
I've have (and use) a couple other Arctic USB fans and have been 100% satisfied with them. This new version (their "USA Edition") has a couple of improvements over past designs.

The base is a metal plate which increases the fan's stability when you're bending the stem to point the fan. The on/off/speed dial switch no longer has a lit LED ring around it. I never found the lit LED ring to be bothersome on the other Arctic fans, so having or not having it is not a big deal to me.

The base also does away with the USB hub connections that other models have. That's keeps the base more streamlined and allows it to have a lower profile. It also does away with the clam shell packaging, instead using a very easy to open box.

The build quality of this, like the other Arctic fans I have, is excellent. The stem is bendy by stays put where you want it; the operating sound is pretty hushed; the on/off/speed control works well. The overall design is attractive, with a red/white/blue color scheme and graphics.

It moves a surprising amount of air. No, it won't blow your hair back as a Vornado fan will, but this makes a noticeable difference in circulating air. The size makes it very easy to find a spot on your desk to position it.

While I can't speak to the long-term reliability of this as of yet, I expect it will last for some time. I have an Arctic fan similar to this that I've been using almost daily for the past 1+ years, and it still works as good as it did when new.

Looks good, works well, and easy to use. Highly recommend.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: ARCTIC Breeze Pro USB Desktop Fan with 4-Port USB Hub

Dell 27 LED Backlit LCD Monitor SE2719H IPS Full HD 1080p, 1920x1080 at 60 Hz HDMI VGA, Black I’m using this Dell 27” monitor with a MacBook Pro. While the monitor offers VGA and HDMI connections, only a VGA cable is included. The product description left out that detail.

The main product picture currently being used shows a silver stand; the stand is actually black as shown in other product photos. I can’t really say if the design of the stand frees up more desk space or not since that’s never been a problem for me, but I do like that it’s a flat base. The viewing angle is adjustable but not the height of the monitor.

I also like the slim power cord! No huge brick adaptor for this monitor.

The main complaint I have with this monitor is how it bounces on my desk. I use a mechanical keyboard, and the monitor bobbles with every keystroke. I have a larger monitor that doesn’t have this problem, so I imagine it’s due to the small stand on the Dell.

Image quality seems to be pretty good. There’s not a ton of options on the monitor, but you can adjust contrast/brightness, and there are presets for “ComfortView” (blue light blocking), Movie, Game, Warm, Cool, and the ability to set a custom color.

When I use it with my laptop, I do my main work on the Dell screen instead of the Mac’s, which is the opposite of what I usually do. And not because of the increased screen size, but because I prefer the image quality.

It arrived in a slightly wider than normal filter box. The box was slightly larger because the filter was packed in a latching plastic box with foam protecting the filter from damage. I looked at the filter under a magnifying light, and it was flat and smooth with no scratches or oddities. It fit my 45-150mm lens perfectly, and it really is a low profile filter. GoPro Hero5 Session The video quality of the camera is pretty good, but the deal breaker for this GoPro is the horrible Capture iphone/mobile app. In order to use the iPhone Capture app to preview images and change the various image/video settings, you must register an account with GoPro before the Capture app will connect with the GoPro Hero Session. By itself it isn't a show stopper, but the Capture app automatically logs you out of the account every week or so, seemingly at random - the major problem with this it requires an internet connection/wifi/cell access to login again. The brilliant engineers at GoPro didn't think of this and realize that people tend to use their GoPros in remote places that won't always have internet access/wifi like backcountry skiing, or far from shore snorkeling or scuba diving.

Another major issue with the camera is on a 32GB memory card, up to 3-4GB is used up saving the .LRV files for the previews and there are no options to turn the creation of those files off.
text_fidelity_b: GoPro Hero5 Session

If you are thinking of wall mounting this device you'd do better by buying a small platform/shelf to place it on. The indicator light is on the bottom. This gets hid easily by the various Echo Dot wall mounts. Like all Echo Dots, they are great to control smart devices but get very poor marks in understanding the elderly and those slow of speech. As one who is elderly, wears dentures, and hard of hearing, I don't get my words pronounced with distinction. Echo will usually respond with something it found on the web that has zero relation to what I asked of it. My wife is slow of speech and the echo will cut her off and try to process the fragment without waiting for her to complete. I have submitted a request to Amazon about this to have a final key word to denote end of speech but they have not made any changes to the software, nor replied to my comments.
Overall it is a worthwhile device to have. With as many smart devices that we have to simplify our life this has been a Godsend. However, its impatient teen attention span is annoying when trying to issue commands or to have it actually find something on the web...like we asked.

text_fidelity_a:
Altec Lansing iMW555-BLK Inmotion Bluetooth Speaker Beyond the way it looks, it's relatively easy to pair via Bluetooth, you can charge your phone via USB or NFC, the wireless near-field connection scheme. I'd have given a tooth for an external speaker like this back in the 80s, when battery-powered speakers for the Sony Walkman existed. It's more than adequate for a dorm room or office space, it's lightweight, it seems to be pretty durable, each of the EIGHT speakers have a metal screen protecting the cones. CX -- No, I was wrong, there are NOT eight speakers, there are FOUR speakers, plus four extra cones which amplify the sound. I counted the grilles and assumed they were all speakers. My error!

This comes in a beautiful package, it would make a fantastic gift. It promises up to 8-10 hours of play, which is more than decent. There's a Mic In jack, which I'm somewhat baffled by, and an Aux jack, which is very handy if you own an older non-Bluetooth iPod. There's a Talk button for use with your phone. I'm unclear how that would function. This can be mounted on a wall, AND THEY INCLUDED THE WALL ANCHORS AND SCREWS. Very thoughtful.

The main thing, the sound quality, is better than I've heard with other Bluetooth speaker solutions, which, honestly, is not saying that much. I'm looking for a software EQ on my iPhone and I don't find one. I don't want to ask for the Moon, but an EQ on the speaker would be worth more to me than the NFC charging scheme.

A very good Bluetooth speaker solution. It looks gorgeous, it's easily paired, the sound is relatively bright and clear. Room-filling sound. It won't replace home stereos, but that's not what it's meant to do. Anyone young enough to NOT remember how good vinyl LPs sound will be positively thrilled with this device!

---

This device actually sounds better filling a room with sound than it does just sitting on your desk. For whatever that's worth. It sounds better if it's not right under your nose.

---

This device does match up with my iPhone very well, and without a lot of fuss or headaches like other Bluetooth solutions I've tried. If I can't get each device to sniff one another's butt, I lose interest pretty quickly. This device matches up on its own and easily, so that's a major plus.
text_fidelity_b: Altec Lansing iMW555-BLK Inmotion Bluetooth Speaker

[Upgraded Version] Anker USB 3.0 SuperSpeed 10-Port Hub Including a BC 1.2 Charging Port with 60W (12V / 5A) Power Adapter [VIA VL812-B2 Chipset and Updated Firmware 9081] AH231 After having to practically rip the box to get this thing open, I set it up with my computer. The plug into the transformer is a little tight and I'm not sure it is entirely in. Though it's not moving. The computer did not recognize it at first. I do have a Sabrent 7 port hub plugged in to another USB slot on my laptop, but that is mostly filled with devices that are required for license verification (ilok, etc...) and it will only really take a powered hard drive even though it is powered.

Back to the Anker. I plugged in 2 Seagate 2 TB drives and a WD 2 TB drive, all bus powered. Once the computer finally recognized the Anker (I had to take the USB out and plug it back in) All three drives were quickly recognized. However after about 10 minutes I got a message that the last USB device I plugged in wasn't working and then the drives reconnected, except the WD This is the same behavior I was getting with my Sabrent that caused me to look for another hub. I was able to reconnect the WD by unplugging it a replugging it in. It is getting to be a very frustrating thing trying to find a USB 3.0 hub that can handle multiple drives.

I am running Windows 8 on an HP laptop. I will try this for a bit. I hope it doesn't have to go back because I had to damage the packaging to open it.

Update 12/2/16 - I've had this for 2 years. for the last year it has been a pain to use. The plug that was difficult to plug in now won't stay in. It turns off if I slightly move it. I'm looking for another one. Most of the spots are taken up by USB licensers, so when it stops working, it crashes my programs. very frustrating.
Updated 1/6/15: After keeping this plugged in, it is now working okay. I am not sure that some of the problems are not caused by my HP shutting the USB ports down as a power saver. I transferred a number of files from the WD to the Seagate using the Anker with no issues. It was actually very quick. However, I only had the 2 drives attached. I'm not sure there is anything out there that is any better. This is my 4th USB 3.0 hub I've tried and none of them really work well. And it could be my computer. But the whole point of a powered hub is that the computer doesn't have to support it.

7/16/16 Update
Still using this, but the plug doesn't like to stay in. I have to be very careful not to knock it out. Otherwise, it is still working well.
text_fidelity_b: [Upgraded Version] Anker USB 3.0 SuperSpeed 10-Port Hub Including a BC 1.2 Charging Port with 60W (12V / 5A) Power Adapter [VIA VL812-B2 Chipset and Updated Firmware 9081] AH231

text_fidelity_a:
ProElife Ultra Thin Silicone Full Size Keyboard Cover Skin for 2017 2018 Apple iMac Magic Keyboard with Numeric Keypad MQ052LL/A A1843 US Layout (Item Folded in Packaging) (Ombre Blue) UPDATE (12/25/2021):

I have removed this skin (bought on January 27, 2020) for 3 reasons.
1. The keys were not so visible below the skin because it has become more translucent instead of remaining transparent.
2. The shift key on the left side was ripped from being used and from my fingernail, I would think. IOW, it's not so tough.
3. A sticky liquid has formed between my keyboard and the skin. I removed it with more than just wiping. No solvent has been used at any time. Perhaps the silicone reacted with the plastic keys. Nothing has ever been spilled on the keyboard. Still, I have a skin on the keyboard as protection against any liquid OR dust OR hair getting into my keyboard that I have been using since 2008 when it was new.

My replacement (Allinside) is now in place and I can once again see the keys.
The skin fits the keys such that it does NOT have to wrap around the edges of the keyboard.

UPDATE (7/14/2018): After one year I have to replace this keyboard skin because it is wearing out in several places, mainly the left side command key where there is a ¼ inch slit. When I have to type a long document / letter, I remove the skin so I can type faster on the aluminum keyboard because the keys require only a light touch. I have not switched to a BT keyboard because this one is so good, and the fact that it is wired is not a problem with a little tape to keep the cable out of the way when I slide the keyboard shelf in and out. The skin I received is transparent with nothing printed on any of the keys.

For those who have the wired Apple aluminum extended keyboard (with keypad), this product fits correctly to protect the keyboard from dust and spills. It is in use on my Mac Pro (early 2008). The description says for iMac, but it fits any of these keyboards of this style, not just the iMac keyboard.

Winegard HD8200U Platinum VHF/UHF HDTV Antenna (65 Miles+, Digital, 4K Ultra High-Def Ready) First, be aware this beast is more than 14 feet long and about 9 feet wide when unfolded and assembled. It does move in the wind. It doesn't weigh that much, but with so many elements forming such a large device it becomes a sail.

I mounted it on a 10' length of 1-1/4" electrical conduit held to a tall garage wall using [[ASIN:B001RCMEEA Channel Master CM-9025 3-Inch Heavy-Duty Wall Mount for TV Antenna Masts]]. The antenna is about 23 feet in the air.

The HD8200U has a very high-gain, directional Yagi UHF antenna on the front and a full VHF antenna on the rear. I really don't think I need the VHF section and may retire this antenna and opt for a more compact UHF Yagi if the high winds we occasionally experience cause trouble. After assembly, the two sections feed into an electronics box using 1/8" aluminum rods from each section. You then mechanically attach a top plate to the box that connects to all four aluminum leads. The coax connector is in this top plate. A weather boot is supplied to seal the connection.

The HD8200U does bring in the signal like a champ. My stations are at least 19 miles and 68 miles away. It's very directional. If I aimed 30 degrees off, I got zero channels. Check where your stations are broadcast from using www.antennaweb.org (antennaweb dot org) which provides distance and direction in degrees from magnetic north using your zip code. Very handy.
text_fidelity_b: Winegard HD8200U Platinum VHF/UHF HDTV Antenna (65 Miles+, Digital, 4K Ultra High-Def Ready)
